Sensitivity Analysis for Sample Size Planning From the AIPE Perspective for the Mean of a Crossed Design of Units and Raters

Source: R/ss_aipe_crossed_sensitivity.R
ss_aipe_crossed_sensitivity.Rd

Shows by Monte Carlo simulation what a plan from ss_aipe_crossed delivers when the true variance components differ from the planning values. The design is either planned from the supposed components, as a researcher would plan it, or fixed by the user; complete arrays of that size are then drawn from the population with the true components, the interval of ci_crossed is formed from each, and the realized widths and the coverage of the true mean are summarized. A planning value of the rater component that is too small is the costly mistake in this design, since that component sets the floor below which no number of units can bring the interval.

Usage

ss_aipe_crossed_sensitivity(
  true_var_unit,
  true_var_rater,
  true_var_residual,
  supposed_var_unit = NULL,
  supposed_var_rater = NULL,
  supposed_var_residual = NULL,
  specified_n_units = NULL,
  specified_n_raters = NULL,
  width,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  assurance = NULL,
  n_raters = NULL,
  unit_cost = 0,
  rater_cost = 0,
  judgment_cost = 1,
  quantile = c("t", "normal"),
  max_units = 1e+05,
  max_raters = 500,
  true_grand_mean = 0,
  G = 1000,
  print_iter = FALSE,
  filename = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

true_var_unit, true_var_rater, true_var_residual

The data generating variance components of the unit effects, the rater effects, and the residuals (see ss_aipe_crossed). The first two must be nonnegative and the third positive.

supposed_var_unit, supposed_var_rater, supposed_var_residual

The supposed variance components, the planning values the design is planned from (not estimates computed from data), all three together. Supply these or specified_n_units and specified_n_raters, but not both.

specified_n_units, specified_n_raters

A design to evaluate (whole numbers of at least 2, both together) in place of a planned one; the planner is then bypassed.

width

Desired full width of the confidence interval for the mean, against which the realized widths are judged.

conf_level

Confidence level of the interval (default 0.95).

assurance

Optional assurance, strictly between 0 and 1, passed to ss_aipe_crossed when the design is planned; echoed in the output when supplied, with a specified design as well.

n_raters, unit_cost, rater_cost, judgment_cost, quantile, max_units, max_raters

Passed to ss_aipe_crossed when the design is planned, and unused with a specified design.

true_grand_mean

The data generating mean (default 0). The widths and the coverage do not depend on it; it sets the scale of the reported estimates.

G

Number of Monte Carlo replications (default 1000).

print_iter

Logical. Print the replication index as the simulation runs; default FALSE.

filename

Optional path of a CSV file to receive the per-replication results (the grand mean, the two limits, the width, the degrees of freedom, and the two tail misses), appended when the file already holds a table and created otherwise; the default NULL writes nothing, and a throwaway run that wants the file should point it at tempfile(fileext = ".csv").

seed

Optional integer seed. The default NULL draws from, and advances, the current random number stream; an integer makes the call reproducible, and the caller's random number state is restored when the call returns.

Value

A data.frame (class dmar_tbl) with rows mean_grand_mean, median_grand_mean, and sd_grand_mean (summaries of the \(G\) estimates); mean_ci_width, median_ci_width, and sd_ci_width (of the realized widths); pct_ci_less_width (the proportion of intervals no wider than width); pct_ci_miss_low (the proportion lying entirely above the true mean), pct_ci_miss_high (entirely below it), and total_type_I_error (their sum); mean_df (the mean Satterthwaite degrees of freedom); and the echoes n_units and n_raters (the design evaluated), the three true_var_* and three supposed_var_* components (the latter NA for a specified design), true_grand_mean, width, conf_level, and assurance when one was supplied. The proportions are on the 0 to 1 scale.

Details

Each replication draws \(n_u\) unit effects, \(n_r\) rater effects, and \(n_u n_r\) residuals from normal distributions with the true variances, forms the complete array, and computes the interval exactly as ci_crossed does: the ANOVA estimates of the components, negative ones truncated at zero, plugged into the variance of the grand mean, with Satterthwaite (1946) degrees of freedom. The summary separates two sources of error: the planning values (compare a well specified run with a misspecified one) and the approximations of the plan itself (a well specified run whose pct_ci_less_width is well below one half, or below the assurance, or whose coverage is far from conf_level; a plan without an assurance meets its width somewhat more than half the time, as ss_aipe_crossed explains). A plan with quantile = "normal" shows the second kind, since its target ignores the t quantile the interval uses; with a rater component at or near zero it can fall far short.

The record of the simulation

Every sensitivity function of the package summarizes its replications over one denominator: the replications that produced a confidence interval (for a power sensitivity function, a test). The proportion of intervals that met the width target (pct_ci_less_width), the proportions of intervals that missed the true value, and the summaries of the widths are all taken over those replications. A replication without an interval is in none of these rows. It is counted, and the returned table carries the counts in its attribute simulation, a list read with attr(x, "simulation"):

attempted

the number of replications asked for (G).

returned

the number that produced an interval (a test).

failed

the number that did not (attempted - returned).

denominator

the number of replications the rows named above are taken over, which is returned.

width_target_probability

the proportion of the replications with an interval whose interval met the width target, the value of the pct_ci_less_width row; NA for a function or a call without a width target, and when no replication produced an interval.

width_target_mc_ci

the exact binomial (Clopper-Pearson) limits for that proportion, at the confidence level of the table. They describe the error of the simulation, which shrinks as G grows, and nothing else.

A function that records more about its run adds elements to the list, and its help page names them. The line "Replications" beneath the printed table gives G, and the three counts when a replication was without an interval. With many replications without an interval the rows describe only the studies in which the interval could be formed, so failed is to be reported beside them.

References

Satterthwaite, F. E. (1946). An approximate distribution of estimates of variance components. Biometrics Bulletin, 2(6), 110–114. doi:10.2307/3002019

Examples

# G = 200 keeps the example quick; a reported study deserves the
# default G = 1000 or more. The first plan on the help page of
# ss_aipe_crossed(), evaluated when its planning values are right:
ss_aipe_crossed_sensitivity(
  true_var_unit = 0.50, true_var_rater = 0.10, true_var_residual = 0.40,
  supposed_var_unit = 0.50, supposed_var_rater = 0.10,
  supposed_var_residual = 0.40,
  width = 0.40, G = 200, seed = 113)
#>  term                  value 
#>  mean_grand_mean       -0.015
#>  median_grand_mean     -0.003
#>  sd_grand_mean         0.103 
#>  mean_ci_width         0.396 
#>  median_ci_width       0.395 
#>  sd_ci_width           0.033 
#>  pct_ci_less_width     0.555 
#>  pct_ci_miss_low       0.010 
#>  pct_ci_miss_high      0.040 
#>  total_type_I_error    0.050 
#>  mean_df               75.376
#>  n_units               94    
#>  n_raters              22    
#>  true_var_unit         0.500 
#>  true_var_rater        0.100 
#>  true_var_residual     0.400 
#>  supposed_var_unit     0.500 
#>  supposed_var_rater    0.100 
#>  supposed_var_residual 0.400 
#>  true_grand_mean       0     
#>  width                 0.400 
#>  conf_level            0.950 
#> 
#> Replications: 200
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%

# The same plan when the raters in fact differ twice as much as
# planned: nearly every interval is now wider than the target, since
# the design has too few raters for the larger rater component.
ss_aipe_crossed_sensitivity(
  true_var_unit = 0.50, true_var_rater = 0.20, true_var_residual = 0.40,
  supposed_var_unit = 0.50, supposed_var_rater = 0.10,
  supposed_var_residual = 0.40,
  width = 0.40, G = 200, seed = 113)
#>  term                  value

#>  true_var_rater        0.200
